question: SGLT2 inhibitors (e.g., empagliflozin) are safe and fully effective at reducing HbA1c in patients with an eGFR of 25 mL/min/1.73m².

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. SGLT2 inhibitors lower glucose by inducing glycosuria — a mechanism that requires adequate glomerular filtration. At eGFR <30-45 mL/min/1.73m² (threshold varies by agent), glucose-lowering efficacy is substantially reduced. Always check eGFR before prescribing.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. SGLT2 inhibitors require adequate renal function to exert their glucose-lowering effect (glucosuria). At eGFR <30 (for glucose-lowering) or <45 mL/min/1.73m² (class-dependent threshold), glycaemic efficacy is lost. However, cardiorenal benefit may persist at lower eGFR — check current ADA guidelines for specific thresholds.
